classification.habit: Perennial sub-scandent shrub, 1–2 m tall, with spreading branches.
classification.habitat: Open and shady places, hedges and waste ground; also cultivated.
classification.distribution: Throughout India in the wild state and occasionally cultivated in gardens.

identification.description: Cylindrical brownish-grey roots with striations and rootlet scars, acrid biting persistent burning taste causing intense tingling on tongue, distinct pungent odor.
identification.whole_plant: Straggling shrub with alternate ovate leaves and spikes of white flowers bearing sticky glandular calyces.
identification.root: Roots 30 cm or more long and about 6 mm or more thick, reddish to deep brown with rootlet scars; bark thin and brown; odour disagreeable; taste acrid.
identification.stem: Woody at base, branches striate, glabrous, somewhat climbing.
identification.leaf: Simple, alternate, ovate to oblong, 3–8 cm long, entire, with a short amplexicaul petiole.
identification.flower: White, in elongated terminal spikes; calyx tubular, covered with stalked sticky glands; corolla salver-shaped with a long slender tube.
identification.fruit: Oblong, five-furrowed capsule enclosed in the persistent glandular calyx.
identification_points: Cylindrical brownish-grey roots with striations and rootlet scars, acrid biting persistent burning taste causing intense tingling on tongue, distinct pungent odor.

therapeutics.anupana: Takra (buttermilk), especially in Arsha and Grahani.
therapeutics.precautions: Use only after shodhana (e.g. in lime water). Fresh root is vesicant and irritant; avoid prolonged contact. Use measured doses as it is tikshna and ushna.
therapeutics.contraindications: Contraindicated in pregnancy (classically abortifacient), in Pitta-predominant states, Amlapitta, Raktapitta and peptic ulcer.

phytochemistry.chemical_notes: The root contains naphthoquinones, chiefly plumbagin, which accounts for its pungent, vesicant and pharmacological activity.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Ignites digestive fire, used in weight loss and ama digestion.
modern_information.safety_notes: Plumbagin is irritant and can be toxic in high doses; the drug is used only after shodhana and in small doses, and avoided in pregnancy.
